q: What is considered the most important innovation in asphalt shingles?
n: Per the MST answer key: Moss resistance.

q: Which component makes asphalt shingles waterproof?
n: The asphalt saturant and coating shed water.

q: Which roofing uses marine plywood as an underlayment and needs heat to seal?
n: Shingle self-seal strips bond with heat.

q: What roof slope suits asphalt shingles?
n: Per the MST answer key: Steep.

q: What fastens GI roofing sheets to steel purlins?
n: Tek screws drill and tap into steel purlins.

q: Where is GI flashing NOT typically needed?
n: Lapped sheets seal by overlap; flashing is for junctions.

q: What is the usual remedy for an overflowing valley gutter?
n: An undersized gutter needs more capacity.

q: What is the most common roofing in the Philippines?
n: Corrugated GI dominates.

q: What is a common mistake in roofing installation?
n: Bad flashing at junctions causes most leaks.

q: What is the ideal roofing for a warehouse?
n: Long-span sheets cover big spans cheaply.

q: What is suitable roofing for a sidewalk canopy?
n: Per the MST answer key: Curvilinear sheet.

q: What type of roofing material is best suited for a rest house located near the beach?
n: Per the MST answer key: Asphalt shingles.

q: What roof type best suits the Philippine climate?
n: Hip roofs resist typhoon winds and shade all walls.

q: What is the most effective roof insulation arrangement?
o: Roof sheet, an air gap, then foil insulation
Roof sheet with foil directly underneath
Roof sheet, foil, then an air gap
n: Reflective foil works when it faces an air space.

q: Where is roof insulation best placed?
o: Above the purlins, below the roof sheet
n: Blankets laid over purlins under the sheet are standard practice.

q: What is the main purpose of the air gap in a roof insulation system?
n: The gap lets foil block radiant heat.

q: Which insulation reflects radiant heat from roofing?
n: Foil has low emissivity.

q: Which roof color absorbs the least heat in the tropics?
n: White reflects the most solar energy.

q: What is the ideal roofing for a greenhouse?
n: It lets light through and resists impact.

q: What do polycarbonate suppliers often fail to mention?
o: Water wicks into the cells, letting moss grow
n: Twin-wall sheets trap water in their flutes.

q: What is a major advantage of polycarbonate roofing for greenhouses?
o: It diffuses natural light while filtering UV
n: UV-coated sheets admit diffused light.

q: Which polycarbonate is most used in greenhouses?
n: Multi-wall sheets insulate and diffuse light.

q: What should be avoided when installing polycarbonate roofing?
n: Over-tightening cracks the sheet and stops thermal movement.

q: Which roof has two slopes on every side?
n: A mansard has a steep lower and a flatter upper slope on all sides.

q: Which roof design typically forms a 45-degree angle?
n: Per the MST answer key: Hip.

q: Which roof has two sloping sides meeting at a ridge?
n: A gable has two slopes and two gable ends.

q: Which roof has a single slope, often used for extensions and minimalist houses?
n: A shed (lean-to) roof has one slope.

q: Which roof has four sloping sides and resists strong winds well?
n: Hip roofs have no tall gable walls to catch wind.

q: What is an advantage of cement and clay roof tiles?
n: They are non-combustible.

q: What type of roofing is made of thermoplastic material that bonds under heat?
n: Per the MST answer key: Asphalt shingles.

q: Which roofing is typical of Mediterranean or Spanish-style architecture?
n: Barrel clay tiles define the style.

q: What is a major disadvantage of ceramic roof tiles?
n: Tiles need a stronger roof frame.
